paragraphs: DUB-1 turns the M-VAVE FM-1 into a generative dub techno machine. It plays itself from the moment it's switched on: chord stabs through a resonant low-pass into a tape echo, short FM pings on loops of unequal length, a sub bass on one of five grooves, a four-on-the-floor kick that ducks the rest, a shaker and an open hat, and a bed of vinyl crackle. An eight-bar arrangement takes the kick out for a break, thins the layers and brings them back with a fill, and now and then a stab is thrown into the echo. You don't play it, you steer it: pick a piece and a scale, take notes out, sweep the…
DUB-1 is a fork of AMB-1, Charles Vestal's generative ambient firmware for the FM-1, and keeps its platform, its panel and much of its sound engine.

Installing it is at your own risk, though it's hard to get stuck: the web installer and M-VAVE's own updater can put the stock firmware back, and an FM-1 that fails to start twice comes up in a safe mode that the installer can reach.
